scientific_question: For the specified chiral cyclopentadienone–iron catalyst C_A, explain how H2 hydrogenates phenyl(trimethylsilyl)methanone to its chiral silyl alcohol, what controls turnover, and how catalyst organization influences formation of the two enantiomers. Predict the favored absolute configuration for this acylsilane.

historical_record.scientific_question: For the specified chiral cyclopentadienone–iron catalyst C_A, explain how H2 hydrogenates phenyl(trimethylsilyl)methanone to its chiral silyl alcohol, what controls turnover, and how catalyst organization influences formation of the two enantiomers. Predict the favored absolute configuration and determine how replacing Si(CH3)3 with C(CH3)3 changes enantiomer discrimination on the same catalyst.

inputs.content: Primary substrate: phenyl(trimethylsilyl)methanone, Ph–C(=O)–Si(CH3)3; SMILES O=C(c1ccccc1)[Si](C)(C)C. The carbonyl carbon is bonded directly to silicon, not to a methylene spacer. Matched substrate for the structural comparison: 2,2-dimethyl-1-phenylpropan-1-one, Ph–C(=O)–C(CH3)3; SMILES O=C(c1ccccc1)C(C)(C)C. Only the Si(CH3)3-to-C(CH3)3 substitution defines this substrate comparison.

Primary product: phenyl(trimethylsilyl)methanol, Ph–CH(OH)–Si(CH3)3; constitutional SMILES OC(c1ccccc1)[Si](C)(C)C. The carbinol carbon bears phenyl, hydroxyl, hydrogen and trimethylsilyl. Comparison product: 2,2-dimethyl-1-phenylpropan-1-ol, Ph–CH(OH)–C(CH3)3; constitutional SMILES OC(c1ccccc1)C(C)(C)C. Both alcohol enantiomers are in scope. No major-product absolute configuration is supplied; assign any claimed stereochemical outcome from an explicit molecular structure.

Reacting catalyst C_A is a neutral cyclopentadienone–iron tricarbonyl complex. Define the ligand graph by the ring C1(=O)–C2=C3–C4=C5–C1, with an additional C3–CH2–CH2–CH2–CH2–C4 bridge. Thus the fused ring has six members. C2 and C5 each attach directly to the stereogenic C2 of a pyrrolidine ring; both pyrrolidine C2 stereocenters are S. Each pyrrolidine nitrogen is bonded to S(=O)2–Ar, where Ar is 4-phenylphenyl, with sulfur attached at aryl C1 and phenyl at C4. The iron is coordinated to the four diene carbons of the cyclopentadienone and bears three terminal carbon-bound CO ligands. This specifies the starting molecular identity, not an optimized conformation or electronic state. Direct experimental comparison for C_A uses substrate 0.2 mmol, catalyst 2 mol %, trimethylamine N-oxide 4 mol %, toluene 0.3 mL, H2 30 atm, 80 °C, 12 h. A distinct comparison catalyst C_B has the same ligand backbone and S,S stereochemistry, but Ar is 3,5-di-tert-butyl-4-methoxyphenyl, with sulfur attached at aryl C1. The optimized aryl-acylsilane comparison conditions for C_B are substrate 0.5 mmol, catalyst 2 mol %, trimethylamine N-oxide 4 mol %, H2 30 atm, iPrOH/H2O 1.2:0.3 mL, 60 °C, 12 h. C_B is observational context only: its performance must not be relabelled as a measurement for C_A, and calculations on C_B are not a required outcome.

With C_A under its toluene/H2 conditions in PI3, the primary substrate gave its alcohol in 87% yield and 86:14 enantiomeric ratio. With C_B under its optimized iPrOH/H2O/H2 conditions in PI3, the primary substrate gave its alcohol in 95% yield and 93:7 enantiomeric ratio. The tert-butyl analogue showed lower enantiomer discrimination in experiments with related catalysts, but no matched numerical C_A measurement for that analogue is supplied. This is contextual evidence, not a same-catalyst quantitative selectivity datum. Yields and enantiomeric ratios are observations, not calculated answers or rate constants; no concentration-versus-time data are supplied.

Provide calculation-supported answers for:

1. The chemical account of hydrogenation and productive catalyst return.
2. A comparison identifying the conditional turnover bottleneck.
3. The primary alcohol formation preference with explicit product structures/CIP assignments.
4. The explanation connecting catalyst organization to this discrimination.

Report the relevant numerical energies and comparisons with their reference components, units, charge/spin, temperature and standard state. Local barriers, overall energy heights and reaction free energies are different quantities.

Evidence requirements follow the claims: transition structures require appropriate frequency and chemical-connectivity checks, and spin-crossing or population claims require corresponding physical evidence. Distinguish a conditional electronic-state pathway from a predicted crossing rate and a single-conformer energy gap from an experimental er. No fixed reaction sequence, hypothesis count, exhaustive pathway search or software is required.
